name: Frostsaber Rock
summary: Frostsaber Rock is a towering stone promontory rising above the snowy northern reaches of Winterspring. It serves as the primary sanctuary and training grounds for the noble frostsaber cats of the region.

sections.title: A Perch in the Tundra
sections.body: Rising high above the frozen wastes of northern Winterspring, Frostsaber Rock commands a sweeping view of the snowbound wild. The crag is named for the fierce, majestic frostsaber predators that prowl the slopes and valleys below. At its highest apex resides Rivern Frostwind, a solitary night elf dedicated to raising and tending these beasts. For champions loyal to the Alliance willing to brave the harsh conditions and prove their devotion, Rivern offers the rare privilege of learning to raise, tame, and ride one of these legendary snowy mounts.

faq.answer: Rivern Frostwind makes his camp at the very summit of the rock. He is a trainer dedicated to the regional frostsaber cats and acts as a mentor for Alliance members seeking to earn a frostsaber companion.

faq.q: Can Horde players train beasts here?
faq.answer: No. Rivern Frostwind offers his training and companion beasts exclusively to trusted allies of the Alliance. Horde travelers will find no welcome on the summit.

faq.q: What creatures are found around the rock?
faq.answer: The icy crag and surrounding plateaus are home to wild frostsaber cats, prowling the snowy terrain alongside other hardy beasts native to the harsh climate of Winterspring.

faq.q: Has anyone notable visited this summit?
faq.answer: The wandering beastmaster Rexxar is known to have traveled across Winterspring and climbed Frostsaber Rock during his solitary wanderings across Kalimdor.

angles.text: Alliance heroes who earn the trust of Rivern Frostwind atop the rock can undertake an arduous path of training to ride the famed Winterspring frostsaber.
The crag and its surrounding slopes offer an inspiring proving ground for hunters seeking to observe some of the fiercest predators native to northern Kalimdor.
